trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Going right would leave both cell (1,6) and cell (3,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up, the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,5). So the line goes left.
Going up, the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,5); going left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1). So the line goes down.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1); going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from cell (4,3)) was wrong, so the line must go down.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down, the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1). So my guess (left from number 3) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Going right would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going down would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down would leave both cell (6,1) and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2). So the line goes left.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Cell (2,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going down would strand number 8: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (5,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
